text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Revenue from privatizations will yield 450 billion escudos in 1997 said Prime Minister Antonio Guterres in a meeting in New York with local bankers.
- Portugal's fuel prices are to rise in October, according to market analysts contacted by the paper.
- Banking operation BCP/Jeronimo Martins (JM) may be repeated in Poland. A source from the retail company said that it plans branches in its retail operations abroad.
- Horacio Roque and British American Tobacco (BAT) maintain their interest in tobacco company Tabaqueira privatisation.
- Government discovers 100 billion escudo error in its 1997 budget calculations due to an overly optimistic calculation for VAT revenues.
- The construction of new motorways by private investors will not occur until the end of 1997. Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho will explain in a cabinet meeeting today the causes of the delay.
- State companies had last year their best ever results but many companies are still showing high losses.

- Portuguese Government warns Spanish Government about the frequent violations of Portuguese waters by Spanish fishing boats. Measures are needed to avoid incidents such as the one in which two Spanish fishermen were hurt last Tuesday.
- Petrol company Petrogal buys from Caixa Geral de Depositos 20 percent of Transgas shares.
- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus sees the Portuguese economy growing between 2.5 and 3.0 percent in 1997.
